_meta.parseCode: MorphGNT 8-slot code: person, tense, voice, mood, case, number, gender, degree.
_meta.attested: true when this exact form+parse occurs in the GNT (validated by build_data.py).

paradigms.title: εἰμί — present (I am)
paradigms.note: Irregular and enclitic, but the most common verb in the NT. Learn it as a song: εἰμί, εἶ, ἐστί(ν), ἐσμέν, ἐστέ, εἰσί(ν).

paradigms.title: εἰμί — imperfect (I was)
paradigms.note: ἦν (he/she/it was) is the 2nd most common form of εἰμί; John 1:1 uses it three times. MorphGNT tags ἤμην as middle.

paradigms.title: εἰμί — future (I will be)
paradigms.note: The future of εἰμί has middle endings with active meaning; ἔσται (it will be) is the one you will meet most.

paradigms.title: εἰμί — present subjunctive
paradigms.note: Just the endings of λύω's subjunctive with a rough breathing: ὦ, ᾖς, ᾖ, ὦμεν, ἦτε, ὦσι(ν).

paradigms.title: ὁ, ἡ, τό — the article
paradigms.note: The single most useful paradigm in Greek: nouns and adjectives of the 1st and 2nd declension share these endings. Learn the article and you have learned the cases.

paradigms.title: λόγος — 2nd declension masculine
paradigms.note: Endings: -ος -ου -ῳ -ον (-ε) / -οι -ων -οις -ους. Compare the article: same vowels, same pattern.

paradigms.title: ἔργον — 2nd declension neuter
paradigms.note: Neuter nominative and accusative are always identical, and the plural of both ends in -α. A neuter plural subject often takes a singular verb.

paradigms.title: ἀρχή — 1st declension in -η
paradigms.note: Feminine nouns in -η keep η through the singular: -η -ης -ῃ -ην. The plural is the same for every 1st-declension noun: -αι -ων -αις -ας.

paradigms.title: ἡμέρα — 1st declension in -α (after ε ι ρ)
paradigms.note: When the stem ends in ε, ι or ρ the α stays through the singular: -α -ας -ᾳ -αν.

paradigms.title: δόξα — 1st declension in -α (mixed)
paradigms.note: Other -α nouns switch to η in the genitive and dative singular: -α -ης -ῃ -αν.

paradigms.title: προφήτης — 1st declension masculine
paradigms.note: A few masculine nouns (προφήτης, μαθητής, Ἰωάννης) use 1st-declension endings but a -ου genitive borrowed from the 2nd declension, and take the masculine article: ὁ προφήτης, τοῦ προφήτου.

paradigms.title: σάρξ, σαρκός — 3rd declension (consonant stem)
paradigms.note: Find the stem from the GENITIVE (σαρκ-), then add -ς -ος -ι -α / -ες -ων -σι(ν) -ας. The nominative singular is often disguised by the final consonant merging with -ς.

paradigms.title: ἄρχων, ἄρχοντος — 3rd declension (-ντ stem)
paradigms.note: Stems in -ντ lose the ντ before σ, lengthening the vowel: ἄρχων, ἄρχουσι(ν). Participles like λύων follow this exact pattern.

paradigms.title: πατήρ, πατρός — family nouns
paradigms.note: πατήρ, μήτηρ, ἀνήρ shorten the stem in the genitive and dative singular (πατρός, πατρί) and have a distinctive dative plural (πατράσι).

paradigms.title: ὄνομα, ὀνόματος — neuters in -μα
paradigms.note: Stem in -ματ. Neuter, so nominative = accusative, and the plural of both is -ματα. Very common: πνεῦμα, σῶμα, ῥῆμα, αἷμα.

paradigms.title: ἔθνος, ἔθνους — neuters in -ος
paradigms.note: Looks like a 2nd-declension masculine but is neuter 3rd declension: the genitive is -ους, the plural -η. Watch the article: τὸ ἔθνος, τὰ ἔθνη.

paradigms.title: πίστις, πίστεως — feminines in -ις
paradigms.note: The -ις / -εως pattern covers many abstract nouns (πίστις, πόλις, δύναμις, κρίσις). Nominative and accusative plural are both -εις.

paradigms.title: βασιλεύς, βασιλέως — masculines in -ευς
paradigms.note: Nouns for roles and offices: βασιλεύς, ἀρχιερεύς, γραμματεύς. Note the -εῖς of the plural nominative and accusative.

paradigms.title: ἀγαθός, -ή, -όν — 2-1-2 adjective
paradigms.note: Masculine like λόγος, feminine like ἀρχή, neuter like ἔργον. An adjective agrees with its noun in case, number and gender, never necessarily in ending.

paradigms.title: αὐτός, -ή, -ό — he, she, it / self / same
paradigms.note: Declined like ἀγαθός except the neuter αὐτό has no -ν. Three uses: plain pronoun (αὐτοῦ = his), intensive with a noun (αὐτὸς ὁ θεός = God himself), identical with the article (ὁ αὐτός = the same).

paradigms.title: ἐγώ — I / we
paradigms.note: The short forms μου, μοι, με are unaccented (enclitic) and far more common than ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ, which are used for emphasis and after prepositions.

paradigms.title: σύ — you / you all
paradigms.note: Singular σύ vs plural ὑμεῖς: English 'you' hides this, Greek never does. ὑμῖν (to you all) is one of the most common words in the letters.

paradigms.title: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this
paradigms.note: The stem starts with τ- except in the nominative masculine and feminine (which start with a rough breathing, like the article). The vowel before the ending matches it: ου before ο/ω-type endings, αυ before α/η-type.

paradigms.title: ἐκεῖνος, -η, -ο — that
paradigms.note: Declined exactly like αὐτός (neuter ἐκεῖνο without -ν). 'That one' in contrast to οὗτος 'this one'.

paradigms.title: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which, that
paradigms.note: The relative pronoun is the article's endings with a rough breathing and an accent, and no τ-. It takes its gender and number from the noun it refers back to, but its CASE from its job in its own clause.

paradigms.title: τίς, τί — who? what? (and τις, τι — someone, something)
paradigms.note: 3rd-declension. With an acute accent on the first syllable it is a question word; unaccented (enclitic) it means someone / a certain / something. Masculine and feminine share one set of forms.

paradigms.title: πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν — all, every, whole
paradigms.note: 3-1-3 pattern: masculine and neuter are 3rd declension (stem παντ-), feminine is 1st declension. Before a noun without the article: 'every'; with the article: 'all / the whole'.

paradigms.title: πολύς, πολλή, πολύ — much, many
paradigms.note: Irregular only in four forms (πολύς, πολύν, πολύ, πολύ); everywhere else the stem is πολλ- with ordinary 2-1-2 endings.

paradigms.title: μέγας, μεγάλη, μέγα — great, large
paradigms.note: Same trick as πολύς: four short irregular forms (μέγας, μέγαν, μέγα, μέγα), otherwise the stem μεγαλ- with 2-1-2 endings.

paradigms.title: εἷς, μία, ἕν — one (and οὐδείς — no one)
paradigms.note: Singular only. Masculine/neuter stem ἑν-, feminine μία. οὐδείς and μηδείς are just οὐδέ/μηδέ + εἷς: οὐδείς, οὐδεμία, οὐδέν.

paradigms.title: λύω — present active indicative
paradigms.note: Primary active endings: -ω -εις -ει -ομεν -ετε -ουσι(ν). Present = ongoing or general action: 'I loose / I am loosing'.

paradigms.title: λύομαι — present middle/passive indicative
paradigms.note: Primary middle/passive endings: -ομαι -ῃ -εται -όμεθα -εσθε -ονται. Same form for middle (I loose for myself) and passive (I am being loosed); context decides. Deponent verbs (ἔρχομαι) use these endings with active meaning.

paradigms.title: ἔλυον — imperfect active indicative
paradigms.note: Augment ἐ- in front + secondary endings -ον -ες -ε(ν) -ομεν -ετε -ον. Imperfect = ongoing or repeated action in the past: 'I was loosing / I used to loose'. Vowel-initial verbs lengthen instead: ἀκούω → ἤκουον.

paradigms.title: ἐλυόμην — imperfect middle/passive indicative
paradigms.note: Augment + secondary middle endings -όμην -ου -ετο -όμεθα -εσθε -οντο. Deponents: ἠρχόμην 'I was coming'.

paradigms.title: λύσω — future active indicative
paradigms.note: Insert σ between stem and the present endings: λύ-σ-ω. Stems ending in a consonant merge with σ: π/β/φ + σ = ψ, κ/γ/χ + σ = ξ, τ/δ/θ drop out.

paradigms.title: λύσομαι — future middle indicative
paradigms.note: σ + present middle endings. Some very common verbs have a future that is middle in form only: γίνομαι → γενήσομαι, ἔρχομαι → ἐλεύσομαι, λαμβάνω → λήμψομαι, εἰμί → ἔσομαι.

paradigms.title: ἔλυσα — first aorist active indicative
paradigms.note: Augment + σα + secondary endings: ἔ-λυ-σα, -σας, -σε(ν), -σαμεν, -σατε, -σαν. Aorist = the action viewed as a whole, a snapshot: usually 'I loosed'. It is the default past tense of narrative.

paradigms.title: ἐλυσάμην — first aorist middle indicative
paradigms.note: Augment + σα + secondary middle endings: -σάμην -σω -σατο -σάμεθα -σασθε -σαντο. Not passive! Aorist middle and passive have separate forms.

paradigms.title: ἔβαλον — second aorist active indicative
paradigms.note: Same endings as the imperfect, but on a DIFFERENT (usually shorter) stem: βάλλω → ἔβαλον, λαμβάνω → ἔλαβον, λέγω → εἶπον, ἔρχομαι → ἦλθον. You learn the stem as vocabulary, not by rule.

paradigms.title: ἐγενόμην — second aorist middle indicative
paradigms.note: Imperfect middle endings on the aorist stem γεν-. ἐγένετο 'it happened / came to be' opens hundreds of NT sentences.

paradigms.title: ἐλύθην — aorist passive indicative
paradigms.note: Augment + θη + ACTIVE-looking secondary endings: -θην -θης -θη -θημεν -θητε -θησαν. Some verbs drop the θ (second aorist passive): γράφω → ἐγράφην, ἀποστέλλω → ἀπεστάλην.

paradigms.title: λυθήσομαι — future passive indicative
paradigms.note: θησ + present middle endings. Built on the aorist passive stem, so learn the sixth principal part and you get this for free.

paradigms.title: λέλυκα — perfect active indicative
paradigms.note: Reduplicate the first consonant with ε (λε-λυ-) and add κα: -κα -κας -κε(ν) -καμεν -κατε -κασι(ν). Perfect = a completed action whose result still stands: γέγραπται 'it stands written'.

paradigms.title: λέλυμαι — perfect middle/passive indicative
paradigms.note: Reduplication + primary middle endings attached directly to the stem (no connecting vowel): -μαι -σαι -ται -μεθα -σθε -νται.

paradigms.title: ἐλελύκειν — pluperfect active indicative
paradigms.note: Rare. Augment (often dropped) + reduplication + κει + secondary endings. Meaning: 'I had loosed'. Most NT pluperfects are ᾔδειν (I knew) and εἱστήκειν (I stood).

paradigms.title: λύω — present active subjunctive
paradigms.note: Lengthen the connecting vowel: ω/ῃ/ῃ/ωμεν/ητε/ωσι(ν). The subjunctive is the mood of possibility; it lives in ἵνα (in order that), ἐάν (if), ὅταν (whenever) clauses and after οὐ μή.

paradigms.title: λύσω — aorist active subjunctive
paradigms.note: Aorist stem (with σ, NO augment) + the same lengthened endings. Looks like the future indicative in the 1st person; the ῃ in the 2nd/3rd singular gives it away.

paradigms.title: λύωμαι — present middle/passive subjunctive
paradigms.note: Lengthened vowel + middle endings: -ωμαι -ῃ -ηται -ώμεθα -ησθε -ωνται.

paradigms.title: λυθῶ — aorist passive subjunctive
paradigms.note: θ + the contracted endings -ῶ -ῇς -ῇ -ῶμεν -ῆτε -ῶσι(ν) (all with a circumflex).

paradigms.title: λῦε — present active imperative
paradigms.note: Only 2nd and 3rd persons exist: λῦε (you sg.), λυέτω (let him), λύετε (you pl.), λυέτωσαν (let them). Present imperative = keep doing / do as a habit. Prohibition: μή + present imperative = stop doing.

paradigms.title: λῦσον — aorist active imperative
paradigms.note: No augment (only the indicative augments): λῦσον, λυσάτω, λύσατε, λυσάτωσαν. Aorist imperative = do it (as a single act). Prohibition uses μή + aorist SUBJUNCTIVE instead: μὴ λύσῃς.

paradigms.title: λύου — present middle/passive imperative
paradigms.note: λύου, λυέσθω, λύεσθε, λυέσθωσαν. Deponents use these: ἔρχου (come!), πορεύεσθε (go!).

paradigms.title: λύθητι — aorist passive imperative
paradigms.note: λύθητι, λυθήτω, λύθητε, λυθήτωσαν. Recognize by the θη: ἐγέρθητι 'be raised!', φοβήθητε 'fear!'.

paradigms.title: Infinitives of λύω (and εἰμί)
paradigms.note: Present -ειν / -εσθαι, aorist -σαι / -σασθαι / -θῆναι, perfect -κέναι / -σθαι; second aorist βαλεῖν, γενέσθαι; εἶναι 'to be'. Tense in an infinitive is aspect, not time.

paradigms.title: εἶναι — to be
paradigms.note: The infinitive of εἰμί.

paradigms.title: βαλεῖν — second aorist infinitive
paradigms.note: Second aorist stem + -εῖν (circumflex): βαλεῖν, λαβεῖν, εἰπεῖν, ἐλθεῖν, ἰδεῖν.

paradigms.title: ποιῶ — -έω contract verb, present active
paradigms.note: ε + ω → ω, ε + ει → ει, ε + ο → ου. Contraction leaves a circumflex where the vowels merged. Outside the present and imperfect the ε lengthens to η: ποιήσω, ἐποίησα.

paradigms.title: ἀγαπῶ — -άω contract verb, present active
paradigms.note: α + ω/ο → ω, α + ει/ῃ → ᾳ. Outside the present the α lengthens to η: ἀγαπήσω, ἠγάπησα.

paradigms.title: πληρῶ — -όω contract verb, present active
paradigms.note: ο + ω → ω, ο + ει → οι, ο + ο → ου. Outside the present the ο lengthens to ω: πληρώσω, ἐπλήρωσα.

paradigms.title: δίδωμι — present active (I give)
paradigms.note: -μι verbs reduplicate with ι in the present (δι-δω-) and add endings straight to the stem: -μι -ς -σι(ν) -μεν -τε -ασι(ν). The stem vowel is long in the singular (δίδω-), short in the plural (δίδο-).

paradigms.title: ἔδωκα — aorist active of δίδωμι
paradigms.note: A 'κ-aorist': ἔδωκα, ἔδωκας, ἔδωκε(ν), ἐδώκαμεν, ἐδώκατε, ἔδωκαν. τίθημι (ἔθηκα) and ἀφίημι (ἀφῆκα) do the same.

paradigms.title: τίθημι — present active (I put, place)
paradigms.note: Same pattern as δίδωμι with the stem θε-/θη-: τίθημι, τίθης, τίθησι(ν), τίθεμεν, τίθετε, τιθέασι(ν).

paradigms.title: ἵστημι — present active (I set, stand)
paradigms.note: Stem στα-/στη- with the reduplication showing as a rough breathing: ἵστημι, ἵστης, ἵστησι(ν), ἵσταμεν, ἵστατε, ἱστᾶσι(ν). Its 2nd aorist ἔστην and perfect ἕστηκα both mean 'I stood / I stand'.

paradigms.title: οἶδα — I know (perfect in form, present in meaning)
paradigms.note: οἶδα, οἶδας, οἶδε(ν), οἴδαμεν, οἴδατε, οἴδασι(ν). Its pluperfect ᾔδειν means 'I knew'. Learn it as its own mini-paradigm.

paradigms.title: λύων, λύουσα, λῦον — present active participle
paradigms.note: 3-1-3: masculine/neuter follow ἄρχων (stem λυοντ-), feminine follows δόξα. 'loosing / while loosing'. The participle of εἰμί (ὤν, οὖσα, ὄν) is just the endings.

paradigms.title: λυόμενος, -η, -ον — present middle/passive participle
paradigms.note: The easiest participle: -όμενος declines exactly like ἀγαθός. Deponents use it: ἐρχόμενος 'coming'.

paradigms.title: λύσας, λύσασα, λῦσαν — first aorist active participle
paradigms.note: σα + the -ντ pattern (no augment: only the indicative augments). Aorist participle usually = action before the main verb: 'having loosed'.

paradigms.title: βαλών, βαλοῦσα, βαλόν — second aorist active participle
paradigms.note: Present-participle endings on the second-aorist stem, with the accent on the ending: ἐλθών (having come), ἰδών (having seen), εἰπών (having said), λαβών (having taken).

paradigms.title: λυσάμενος, -η, -ον — aorist middle participle
paradigms.note: σα + -μενος, declined like ἀγαθός. Second aorist: γενόμενος (having become).

paradigms.title: λυθείς, λυθεῖσα, λυθέν — aorist passive participle
paradigms.note: θε + -ντ endings (masc/neut) or -ῖσα (fem): 'having been loosed'. ἀποκριθείς 'answering' (deponent) starts countless sentences in the Gospels.

paradigms.title: λελυκώς, λελυκυῖα, λελυκός — perfect active participle
paradigms.note: Reduplication + κοτ- stem (masc/neut) or -κυῖα (fem): a state resulting from a past action, 'having loosed / in a loosed state'.

paradigms.title: λελυμένος, -η, -ον — perfect middle/passive participle
paradigms.note: Reduplication + -μένος (accent on the μέ), declined like ἀγαθός. γεγραμμένος 'written', ἠγαπημένος 'beloved'.

paradigms.title: ὤν, οὖσα, ὄν — participle of εἰμί
paradigms.note: Pure endings with a rough breathing: ὤν, ὄντος … The present-active participle endings by themselves.
